weapons.name: Night's Edge
weapons.source: Crafted from Blade of Grass, Muramasa, and your world-evil sword at a Demon or Crimson Altar
weapons.why: This is the big melee goal for the phase because it outclasses other broadswords and stays relevant deep into pre-Hardmode.

weapons.name: Bee Keeper
weapons.why: The released bees add burst and make this one of the strongest bossing swords before Hardmode.

weapons.name: Flamarang
weapons.source: Crafted from an Enchanted Boomerang and Hellstone Bars
weapons.why: If you like the boomerang route, this is the best version available before Wall of Flesh prep takes over.

weapons.name: Amazon
weapons.source: Crafted from Rich Mahogany, Jungle Spores, Stingers, and a Vine
weapons.why: It is the cleanest yoyo progression step if you want to stay on that subclass path.

armor.name: Shadow Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Demonite Bars and Shadow Scales
armor.why: In Corruption worlds this is the signature melee set because the speed bonus makes early swords and yoyos feel much better.

armor.name: Crimson Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Crimtane Bars and Tissue Samples
armor.why: Crimson players get a tankier alternative with life-regen utility that is still excellent for melee.

accessories.name: Obsidian Shield
accessories.source: Combined from Obsidian Skull and Cobalt Shield at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Knockback immunity plus fire-block protection makes this one of the most valuable pre-Hardmode accessories overall.

accessories.name: Shield of Cthulhu
accessories.source: Dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu treasure bag
accessories.why: The dash gives both offense and survivability, especially for melee builds that need to stay in range.

accessories.name: Spectre Boots
accessories.source: Combined from Hermes Boots and Rocket Boots
accessories.why: This is the mobility breakpoint where platforming and boss movement start feeling much more under control.

accessories.name: Feral Claws
accessories.why: The melee speed boost is still a big deal and carries naturally into later melee progression.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: It stays the most universal and reliable early combat buff for melee.

buffs.name: Swiftness Potion
buffs.why: More movement speed means more uptime and fewer mistakes during boss fights.

buffs.name: Regeneration Potion
buffs.why: It smooths out incoming damage during long arena fights and exploration loops.

buffs.name: Sharpening Station
buffs.why: The armor penetration bonus is one of the best class-specific pre-Hardmode melee boosts.

weapons.name: Molten Fury
weapons.why: This is the standout bow of the phase and stays excellent through Wall of Flesh prep.

weapons.name: Phoenix Blaster
weapons.source: Crafted from the Handgun and Hellstone Bars
weapons.why: It is the cleanest gun upgrade once Dungeon access and Hellstone are both online.

weapons.name: Beenades
weapons.source: Crafted from Grenades and Bee Wax
weapons.why: They define several pre-Hardmode boss kills because the damage output is absurd for the effort.

weapons.name: Boomstick
weapons.why: It still hits hard enough to remain worth using if your gun progression is not fully online yet.

armor.name: Platinum Armor
armor.why: Until later ranger-specific armor becomes realistic, high defense remains the safest answer.

armor.name: Jungle Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Jungle Spores, Stingers, and Rich Mahogany
armor.why: It is a viable hybrid set if your run leans more into utility than pure ranged scaling.

accessories.name: Obsidian Shield
accessories.source: Combined from Obsidian Skull and Cobalt Shield at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: It solves knockback and fire-block problems in one slot, which is huge for a ranged class setting up longer fights.

accessories.name: Spectre Boots
accessories.source: Combined from Hermes Boots and Rocket Boots
accessories.why: Ranger feels dramatically better once horizontal and vertical repositioning both improve.

accessories.name: Magic Quiver
accessories.why: Bow builds spike hard with this because the arrow speed and damage bonuses are immediately noticeable.

accessories.name: Shield of Cthulhu
accessories.source: Dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu treasure bag
accessories.why: The dash is still strong for quick spacing corrections and emergency saves.

buffs.name: Archery Potion
buffs.why: Bow-focused ranger setups should almost always have this running.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: More defense gives you room to play imperfectly while still keeping ranged uptime.

buffs.name: Swiftness Potion
buffs.why: It helps kiting, arena recovery, and general boss consistency.

buffs.name: Ammo Reservation Potion
buffs.why: Ammo consumption adds up quickly on the strongest guns, so this stretches your best supplies further.

weapons.name: Space Gun
weapons.why: Meteor Armor turns this into a zero-mana workhorse, which is why the set-and-weapon combo defines the phase.

weapons.name: Demon Scythe
weapons.source: Dropped by Demons in the Underworld
weapons.why: It pierces and deals huge damage when you can aim it well, making it a standout for serious boss prep.

weapons.name: Water Bolt
weapons.why: Its bounce and piercing keep it extremely efficient in arenas and enclosed spaces.

weapons.name: Flower of Fire
weapons.why: This gives you a flexible fireball option if you want a more direct casting rhythm than Water Bolt or Demon Scythe.

armor.name: Meteor Armor
armor.why: This is the defining mage armor here because the Space Gun set bonus completely changes your mana economy.

armor.name: Jungle Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Jungle Spores, Stingers, and Rich Mahogany
armor.why: It remains a strong fallback if you have not committed to the Meteor route.

accessories.name: Mana Flower
accessories.source: Crafted from Nature's Gift and a Mana Regeneration Band
accessories.why: Mage becomes much easier to pilot once potion use is automatic instead of one more thing to manage manually.

accessories.name: Magic Cuffs
accessories.source: Combined from a Mana Regeneration Band and Shackle
accessories.why: The max mana and on-hit mana return are both excellent on longer fights.

accessories.name: Obsidian Shield
accessories.source: Combined from Obsidian Skull and Cobalt Shield at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: It keeps you from getting bullied by knockback while exploring lava-heavy areas and setting up later fights.

accessories.name: Spectre Boots
accessories.source: Combined from Hermes Boots and Rocket Boots
accessories.why: Mobility is still a major survivability multiplier for a fragile class.

buffs.name: Magic Power Potion
buffs.why: The damage bonus is straightforward and strong, which makes it the first mage buff to value consistently.

buffs.name: Mana Regeneration Potion
buffs.why: It reduces downtime and makes spell chains much easier to sustain.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: Even mages need some room for mistakes, and defense is the easiest way to buy it.

buffs.name: Lesser Mana Potion
buffs.source: Crafted from Fallen Stars and Bottled Water
buffs.why: You still want a large stack ready for sustained arena or underworld attempts.

weapons.name: Imp Staff
weapons.why: This is the defining summon of the phase because it stays powerful well beyond the moment you first craft it.

weapons.name: Hornet Staff
weapons.why: It is a strong minion option if your route leans into Queen Bee before full Hellstone progression.

weapons.name: Snapthorn
weapons.why: The whip tag damage is still a huge multiplier, so this remains a core piece of the loadout.

weapons.name: Abigail's Flower
weapons.source: Found growing on grass at night
weapons.why: It is situational, but still worth knowing about because some fights and setups suit it surprisingly well.

armor.name: Obsidian Armor
armor.source: Crafted from Obsidian, Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples, and Silk
armor.why: It is the pre-Hardmode summoner benchmark because the minion and whip bonuses are both excellent.

armor.name: Bee Armor
armor.why: This is the natural alternative when your progression moves through Queen Bee first.

accessories.name: Obsidian Shield
accessories.source: Combined from Obsidian Skull and Cobalt Shield at the Tinkerer's Workshop
accessories.why: Summoner has less margin for getting bounced around, so knockback immunity matters a lot.

accessories.name: Pygmy Necklace
accessories.source: Bought from the Witch Doctor at night in the Jungle
accessories.why: The extra minion slot is one of the highest-value accessories a summoner can equip.

accessories.name: Spectre Boots
accessories.source: Combined from Hermes Boots and Rocket Boots
accessories.why: Mobility continues to solve a lot of early summoner survivability problems.

accessories.name: Shield of Cthulhu
accessories.source: Dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu treasure bag
accessories.why: The dash is especially helpful for a class that often wins by staying alive while summons do the work.

buffs.name: Summoning Potion
buffs.why: An extra minion slot is too important to leave on the table for this class.

buffs.name: Bewitching Table
buffs.why: This station buff is one of the best pre-Hardmode power spikes available to summoner.

buffs.name: Ironskin Potion
buffs.why: Defense still matters because summoner is often punished hardest for every positioning mistake.

buffs.name: Well Fed
buffs.why: It is a low-friction global buff that should be active basically all the time.
